dedupe_keys.name: eia special report natural gas compressor stations on the interstate pipeline network developments since 1996 2007

description: A special report by the US Energy Information Administration, dated 7 November 2007, on compressor stations on the interstate natural gas pipeline network of the lower 48 states. Contents: counts, installed horsepower and throughput capability of mainline compressor stations in 1996 and 2006 (about 1,047 stations, 13.4 million horsepower and 743 billion cubic feet per day rising to 1,201 stations, 16.9 million horsepower and 881 Bcf per day), typical spacing of 50 to 100 miles, average station throughput of about 700 million cubic feet per day and up to 4.6 Bcf per day, and the drivers of change, with 176 new stations, over 250 upgrades, 22 deactivations and 45 downsized stations. Coverage: the US interstate network, 1996-2006. Format and access: web summary and full report. Licence and cost: free federal publication. Caveats: archived figures that have not been updated and no station-level list. Useful for capacity planning and network flow models of gas transmission, for compressor spacing and capacity assumptions. It relates to the case study of electric compressor outages and the Argentine compressor station data in the catalogue.
